source.title: Large to Small Model Stitching Destroys What You Built It to Carry Along the Fit

record.file_problem: The post is present in full, but some equations and model symbols are missing or garbled in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments showing that functional transfer through a fitted bridge can decline while geometric similarity rises, and that transfer depends on bridge objective and weighting. This refines and challenges a simple reading of representation alignment and stitching.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own bridge-fitting and measurement results. Statements about prior work are not recorded as results. No rows are included for proposed future SAE or BPE experiments.
record.test_reason: The post fits affine bridges from a 12.7M to a 0.21M char-level GPT trained on the same data, and reports how much of the large model's advantage survives. That bears on V4 (low-loss linear mapping). It also shows geometric and functional similarity measures diverging, which bears on V6. It does not address scale, modality, seeds, universal features, or the causes of alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right. Add the author's specific point: at α=1 the reconstruction term is underweighted, and balance needs α≈4.8, the activation-variance ratio. The author also stresses this is a toy-scale result whose survival at realistic scale is untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses affine bridges and a cyclic objective related to the cited model-stitching work, but studies training trajectories and functional retention for a toy large-to-small language-model setup rather than only final bridge fit. Two 4-layer char-level models share training data; the author notes that realistic-scale validation is still needed.
record.method_sensitivity: Results change with bridge objective, α weighting, activation scaling, hook point, and whether transfer is measured with a retrained probe or the frozen XS readout.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal α for cyclic bridges tracks the ratio of activation variances between models (about 4.8); rescaling streams to unit RMS achieves the same balance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-to-small linear stitching objectives are implicitly variance-weighted, and their transfer quality depends on balancing source and target activation scales.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer review not stated
record.problems: Toy scale: two 4-layer char-level models with 12.7M and 0.21M parameters, trained on shared data. The author says Finding #1 uses a single seed; no error bars or other uncertainty estimates are reported. Realistic-scale validation is explicitly deferred. Some equations and symbols are missing in the web text, and the accompanying table appears to give 94.3% where the prose gives 94.4%.
record.rows_left_out: None. The post's qualitative claim that the three bridge configurations show the same early-peak-then-decline pattern is represented by the rows with explicit values where available; no additional plot-only values were extracted.

untested.parts: No sweep over size or capability; no different architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
Seeds are used for replication, not to compare learned features across initializations.

Only one large-to-small affine bridge on shared data. No stitching layers, relative representations, unpaired maps, small-to-large direction, or diverse model pairs. Stitched retention is defined but not reported.
No feature or circuit comparison; SAE experiments are only proposed.
No neighbour-count settings, no input-distribution or out-of-distribution variation, and no cross-model convergence measure such as mutual kNN or CKA between unfitted models.
No measurement of alignment plateau across models and no test of shared data or objectives as causes.

missing.what: Arm table: XL round-trip FVU and end retention (α=1: 71.1%; scaled α=1: 82.1%; α=10: 91.5%; α=100: 94.3%), plus drop from peak
Final-layer pre-LayerNorm hook point results (trend only stated)
Retention correlates almost linearly with round-trip survival across α settings

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post with toy models: 4-layer char-level GPTs trained on shared TinyStories data. Finding #1 uses a single seed; Finding #2 uses 3 seeds. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The geometric similarity here is that of a fitted bridge to the target space, not similarity between unfitted models, so the V6 bearing is indirect. V7 links were removed because surplus retention through a width bottleneck does not measure partial convergence or its causes.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model sizes or capability, or comparison across independently trained architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.

The study does not compare features or shared subspaces across seeds of the same architecture. Three seeds are used for some bridge experiments, not to test convergent learning across model initializations.
Tests affine bridging from one larger model to one smaller model, not stitching layers, relative representations, unpaired mappings, or interchangeability across diverse models.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.

Tests changes across functional and geometric measures, bridge objectives, hook points, and loss weights. Does not test alternative neighbour counts, broad input distributions, or out-of-distribution data.

Reports incomplete transfer and cases where geometric and functional measures diverge. The models share training data, but the study does not experimentally test whether shared data or objectives cause alignment, nor compare that explanation with a common model of reality.
